title: Google's Gemini finally lets you keep your chats out of AI training
content_html:
Google quietly adds a way to keep Gemini chats out of AI training

Published Nov 24, 2026, 5:57 PM EST

Timi is the news and deals reporter for Android Police, who has been reporting on technology since 2008. He has worked in tech retail and also the IT space, providing hardware and software support, which gives him a unique perspective on the tech that he covers. This allows him to effectively break down complex subjects into easy-to-read pieces that even casual readers can enjoy. In addition to writing for Android Police, he also makes contributions to XDA covering deals. He also worked as an editor and reporter for Neowin, where he covered news and attended major tech events like CES. He also reviewed phones, tablets, PC products, and other devices. In addition, he also created video content for the Neowin YouTube channel.

Sign in to your Android Police account

Over the past couple of years, we've seen AI do some pretty impressive things. And even if you're not a supporter, there's a pretty good chance you've noticed that it has crept into most apps and services we use every day.

And while it is convenient, the companies delivering these products also have an incentive when it comes to injecting them into as many products as they can, since many use the data to train their AI models to make them better.

As you can imagine, Google isn't an exception here. The brand has been harvesting user data for quite some time, and it's doing so with its AI tools like Gemini as well. The good news is that you can turn off the AI training if you want, you just have to find the option.

A new way to opt out

If you're someone that's always looking to cut down on how much information you share with the apps and services you use, you'll be happy to know that you can now opt out of your chat content when using the Gemini app, while still allowing you to keep your Gemini chat history.

This setting was rolled out before, but 9to5Google now reports that it is making a wider release, which means that you should be on the lookout for it. In order to access this option, you'll need to head to Gemini on the web by navigating to "gemini.google.com" and heading into the Settings menu.

Unlike before, there should be a new “Gemini History” option, which will provide you with new ways to control how your data is used in the Gemini experience. In this section, there will be an option that will allow you to opt out of data collection for "Chat content" which also includes text and attachments.

This will be checked by default, so you'll want to uncheck it to opt out. So, as you can imagine, this is a pretty big deal. You can get the power of Gemini without having to train it with your data. For the most part, we don't think people will have a problem with this new setting. More so, we hope that people will know about it so they can turn training off.

We doubt that Google will go out of its way to let its users know about this new setting, so if you know people, be sure to get the word out. Gemini offers some powerful tools, and it will only continue to get stronger as time passes. While it's hard to say what will happen in the future, there's no choice because it's slowly coming our way. We can only hope for the best.
